output.observation: StoryHearth’s public landing page presents personalised family storybooks, a three-step creation process, pricing and login links, and claims a free digital preview with UK-wide printed hardcover shipping.
output.think_aloud: The service sounds relevant to what I want, but “multimodal generative narrative engine” and “household’s lived-experience corpus” sound deliberately technical rather than reassuring. Before sharing anything about Nikolai, I want to read the privacy information and understand exactly what happens to photographs and personal details.

site_model.who_it_is_for: Families wanting stories featuring their children and other relatives or pets.
site_model.value_proposition: Turn a family memory into a bespoke illustrated storybook that can be previewed digitally and potentially printed as an heirloom.

site_model.fit_for_me: Potentially a good fit because it promises a reassuring story about Nikolai at his new school, but I do not yet trust it enough to enter family information or upload anything.

page_review.purpose: Explain the service, show how creation works, and direct visitors to creation, pricing, privacy, and login.
page_review.what_is_happening: The landing page advertises AI-generated family stories, offers “Proceed” and “See pricing” controls, explains three creation steps, includes testimonials and FAQ links, and provides Privacy, Terms, and Contact links below the fold.
page_review.first_impression: It looks warm and professionally designed, but the jargon in the main description immediately makes me cautious about what data is collected and how it is used.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Not yet. I would inspect Privacy and Terms before creating a story or entering family information.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, I notice “Proceed,” “See pricing,” and the footer links for “Privacy” and “Terms.”
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: “Proceed” is too vague about what happens next, while “See pricing” clearly suggests viewing costs; “Privacy” and “Terms” are the relevant labels for my immediate concern.

issues.title: Overly technical language obscures what is shared with the service
issues.evidence: “Leverage our multimodal generative narrative engine to synthesise bespoke, heirloom-grade story artefacts from your household's lived-experience corpus.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I am being asked to think about my child's data, and corporate jargon does not tell me what information is collected, retained, shared, or used to train AI.
issues.fix: Replace this with plain language, for example: “Tell us about a family memory. We use the details you provide to create a story and illustrations for you only.” Link directly to a clear data-use summary.

issues.title: Main illustration has no accessible description
issues.evidence: [image (no description) 430x440]
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: The image gives no information to anyone using a screen reader and appears unexplained to me visually as well.
issues.fix: Add concise alternative text describing the relevant book-preview illustration, or mark it as decorative if it adds no information.

issues.title: Creation action does not disclose the next step
issues.evidence: [5] link “Proceed →”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I cannot tell whether I will be logging in, uploading photographs, or immediately sharing child data.
issues.fix: Rename the link “Start your story” and state beneath it: “You’ll sign in and enter family details; you can review privacy information first.”

issues.title: Printed price is not visible on the landing page
issues.evidence: “Free digital preview · Printed hardcovers shipped across the UK”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I need to know whether this is a genuinely free service or an expensive printed product before investing time and sharing personal information.
issues.fix: Show a clear “Digital preview: free; hardcover from £X” statement and link to the full price list.

positives: The three-step explanation is easy to scan.
The page explicitly says the digital preview is free.
Privacy, Terms, and Contact links are present without requiring account creation.
The overall design is calm and family-oriented, with no visible countdown or false scarcity.

output.memory_note: Homepage claims a free digital preview and printed hardcovers shipped across the UK.

title: Privacy – StoryHearth

output.observation: The screen is a short privacy notice and terms section stating that StoryHearth processes names, stories and uploaded photographs, may retain images to improve its services, and may use technology partners. It also says digital previews are provided as-is and printed orders are non-refundable once production begins.
output.think_aloud: This is not a privacy notice detailed enough for me. “May be retained,” “may be processed by our technology partners” and “improve our services” do not tell me who the partners are, whether photos train AI, how long they are kept, or how I can get them deleted. I also do not want to upload Nikolai’s photograph until those answers are clear.
output.last_action_feedback: partly — clicking Privacy did load the relevant page, but it did not clearly answer the privacy questions I needed answered before sharing anything.

page_review.purpose: To explain how StoryHearth handles family information, photographs, previews and printed orders.
page_review.what_is_happening: I am viewing a short privacy notice and terms summary. No form or account controls are present, and there is no clear route to request deletion or ask questions about data handling.
page_review.first_impression: I expected a proper privacy policy with specific retention periods, named or clearly described recipients, deletion rights, and details about automated processing. Instead I see broad and potentially alarming wording, so I do not trust it enough to upload a child’s data.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: No. I would not upload Nikolai’s photo or submit his story after reading this.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: I noticed the Privacy, Terms and Contact links, and the Terms link is present, but there is no delete-data control or privacy settings link.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: The heading “Privacy notice” matches the broad goal, but the content does not clearly answer what happens to my child’s information.

issues.title: Data retention and deletion are unspecified
issues.evidence: “Uploaded images may be retained to improve our services”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I need to know how long Nikolai’s photo and story will be kept and whether I can delete them.
issues.fix: State specific retention periods for each type of data, explain when deletion occurs, and provide a clear account or contact process to request deletion.

issues.title: Technology partners are unidentified
issues.evidence: “may be processed by our technology partners”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I cannot assess who can see my child’s photograph or whether it is used for AI training without knowing the recipients.
issues.fix: Name the relevant processors and describe their role, location, data categories, and whether uploaded images or generated content are used to train AI or improve models.

issues.title: Purpose of image processing is too vague
issues.evidence: “to create your book” and “improve our services”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: Creating my book is understandable, but “improve our services” is broad enough that I do not know what secondary use is occurring.
issues.fix: Separate essential processing from optional model training or product improvement, state the purposes plainly, and require an explicit opt-in for any optional use.

issues.title: Terms are not a substitute for full terms
issues.evidence: “Digital previews are provided as-is.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: I need to know what happens if a generated book contains errors or does not meet the agreed description, and I need clear terms before ordering.
issues.fix: Provide complete terms covering preview limitations, errors, corrections, production approval, cancellation, refunds, delivery and customer support.

issues.title: Cancellation and refund limitation is abrupt
issues.evidence: “Printed orders are non-refundable once production begins.”
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: This is a significant restriction and I cannot judge the real cost and risk without knowing the production start point, cancellation rules and what happens if the book is damaged or incorrect.
issues.fix: Explain the exact production stage, show cancellation and refund rules before checkout, and state remedies for damaged, delayed or materially incorrect books.

positives: The page has a clear Privacy heading.
It explicitly mentions names, stories and uploaded photographs.
A Contact link is available.
The wording does not show obvious countdown pressure or a pre-ticked consent box.
page_review.abandon_reason: The privacy notice is too vague about retention, technology partners, AI use and deletion to share sensitive information about my child.

output.memory_note: Privacy page says images may be retained to improve services and processed by unnamed technology partners; printed orders are non-refundable once production begins.
output.plan: I will not upload Nikolai’s photo yet. I will return to My books and see whether the book creation flow can be started without uploading anything, while keeping the missing privacy information in mind.

output.observation: The screen is a short form for identifying the child, describing their appearance, and naming another person in the story. The relationship menu is already set to “Grandparent” even though that has not been chosen by me.

However, “Relationship” is already set to “Grandparent”; I will change that to “Parent” so it accurately describes Mama. I am still cautious about entering personal family details because the privacy notice has not adequately explained retention, AI training, or deletion.

page_review.purpose: Collect basic details about the child and another person before moving on to the family-memory story.
page_review.what_is_happening: The form asks for the child's first name, age, pronouns, optional appearance, another character, and that character's relationship. A “Next” button advances the process.
page_review.first_impression: The form is visually clear and manageable, but I noticed immediately that “Grandparent” is preselected in the relationship menu, making me check that it is not carried forward incorrectly.

walkthrough.q1_would_try: Yes, I would enter the basic character details because the fields match what the story needs.
walkthrough.q2_notice_control: Yes, I noticed the name, age, pronouns, appearance, other-character, and relationship controls, plus the “Next” button.
walkthrough.q3_label_matches_goal: Mostly. “Who else is in the story?” fits, but asking only for a relationship without a specific “Mama” option makes the Parent category feel slightly generic.

issues.title: Relationship is preselected without a choice
issues.evidence: [11] displays “Grandparent” as the selected option before I make a selection.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: A preselected answer can silently put inaccurate information about my family into a personalised story, and it recalls the sort of default choices I distrust.
issues.fix: Default the relationship field to “Select…” and make the user choose a value explicitly.

issues.title: No reminder of data-use limits before personal details
issues.evidence: The form immediately requests a child's name, age, pronouns and appearance, while the only policy information is in the footer links “Privacy” and “Terms”.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: Before entering details about Nikolai, I want a concise reminder of how this information will be used, whether it is used to train AI, and how it can be deleted.
issues.fix: Add a short notice above the form stating what happens to the supplied details, whether they are used for AI training, and how to access or delete them, with a direct link to the full privacy notice.

issues.title: Mother is not named as a relationship option
issues.evidence: [11] offers “Grandparent | Parent | Sibling | Friend | Pet | Other” rather than a specific “Mother” option.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: Mama is a character in our memory, and “Parent” is technically correct but less natural and precise than “Mother.”
issues.fix: Include role-specific choices such as “Mother,” “Father,” or “Parent,” while keeping the categories understandable.

positives: The heading clearly explains the purpose of the form.
The fields are plainly labelled and laid out in a logical order.
The appearance field is explicitly marked optional.
The “Next” button is visually prominent and easy to find.

output.memory_note: On the creation form, the relationship field was preselected as “Grandparent” and had to be changed to “Parent.”
output.plan: I will enter Nikolai's name, age, pronouns and appearance, then add Mama as the other character and explicitly select the Parent relationship before continuing.

page_review.what_is_happening: The page asks the user to optionally upload a clear photo of the child's face. No photo is selected, and the available actions are “Back” and “Create my book.”

issues.title: Photo upload lacks specific privacy disclosure
issues.evidence: “Upload a clear photo of your child's face so the illustrations look like them.” The page itself does not explain whether the image is used for AI training, who can access it, how long it is retained, or how it can be deleted.
issues.why_it_matters_to_me: A child's photograph is sensitive personal information, and I will not upload it without knowing these consequences.
issues.fix: Place a concise disclosure beside the upload stating whether photos train AI, named categories of processors or recipients, retention periods, deletion rights, and whether deleting the book also deletes the original. Link to the detailed privacy notice.

issues.title: File control has no explicit accessible label
issues.evidence: [30] file-upload (no label), with only the native text “Choose file”

issues.title: Footer text has weak contrast

issues.why_it_matters_to_me: Important legal and contact links are difficult to see, particularly when I am specifically checking privacy terms.
issues.fix: Use WCAG-compliant text and link colours with sufficient contrast, and make the targets large enough to activate comfortably.

positives: The heading clearly says the photo is optional, so I do not feel forced to provide it.
The “Back” button allows me to return and review the preceding choices.
